problem: Maximum inner product search over large databases is computationally expensive, requiring fast lookup of database vectors most similar to a query.
approach: Train neural networks to directly predict MIPS solutions by learning the convex value function using Input Convex Neural Networks (ICNNs) or VectorICNNs, amortizing the cost across a query distribution.
contribution: Demonstrates that convexity provides an effective inductive bias, achieving high match rates with only a single forward pass at inference.

problem: Molecular representation learning fails to generalize out-of-distribution when training data covers only limited chemical space and models rely on environment-dependent factors.
approach: Propose MoSIR framework that decomposes molecular embeddings into semantic invariant and environment-sensitive components via prototype constraint and bi-level min-max optimization.
contribution: Consistently outperforms baselines on molecular OOD benchmarks across diverse distribution shifts.

problem: De novo ligand design lacks flexibility in modeling real docking interactions, relies on pseudo objectives rather than true de novo generation, and cannot generate diverse ligand types.
approach: Introduce MagicDock framework using gradient inversion where reverse gradients from binding prediction guide ligand generation, with differentiable 3D point-cloud representations capturing docking details.
contribution: Achieves average improvements across 9 scenarios with theoretical guarantees.

problem: Audio foundation models struggle to process complex multi-source acoustic scenes with multiple speakers and background/foreground sound effects.
approach: AudioChat framework uses LLM-based tool-calling agents to simulate user-system interactions for training data, with Audio Transfusion Forcing objective for structured reasoning and interactive multi-turn understanding.
contribution: Enables unified generation, editing, and understanding of audio stories with three new metrics measuring task performance.

problem: Federated class-incremental learning must balance exemplar effectiveness with privacy while learning new classes without forgetting old ones in distributed settings.
approach: Propose CLIF method using cross-view Lewis weight fusion to compute importance scores from multiple feature perspectives and frequency-based weighted training.
contribution: Consistently improves baselines by 1-6% with theoretical guarantees for soundness.

problem: Graph contrastive learning with artificial perturbations diverges from biological reality when applied to gene regulatory networks, and most methods avoid structural changes entirely.
approach: Propose SupGCL that incorporates biological perturbations from gene knockdown experiments as explicit supervision, linking artificial augmentations with real perturbations.
contribution: Yields clearer disease-subtype structure and improves clustering on patient-derived GRNs from three cancer types.

problem: Traditional TDDE solvers require time discretization, forcing a latency-accuracy trade-off where high fidelity requires prohibitive runtime.
approach: Introduce DS-TS using Dynamical System Machines with excitatory-inhibitory coupling, state-aware nonlinearity, and hierarchical temporal integration for continuous physical evolution.
contribution: Achieves high-fidelity solutions with ~10³× speed and ~10⁵× energy efficiency improvements over baseline solvers.

problem: Static fine-tuning of foundation models like SAM2 imposes rigid structural constraints, limiting adaptability to varying complexity in specialized downstream tasks.
approach: Propose ACO-MoE-LoRA combining Ant Colony Optimization with mixture-of-experts to dynamically evolve expert selection and LoRA ranks during training via pheromone-guided routing.
contribution: Consistently outperforms static adapters on 16 datasets while addressing local optimality limitations of recent dynamic heuristics.

problem: Training-free video anomaly detection suffers from computational inefficiency due to complex memory retrieval or high-latency visual-language models.
approach: Propose PRISM framework using differential amplification and whitening mechanisms to suppress common-mode background noise in embedding space from pre-trained multimodal models.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance among training-free methods with real-time inference capability.

problem: Masked diffusion language models require expensive iterative denoising by repeatedly processing the entire sequence at every step.
approach: Propose DyLLM that selectively computes only salient tokens by identifying them via cosine similarity of attention contexts, reusing cached activations for other tokens.
contribution: Achieves up to 9.6× higher throughput while preserving baseline accuracy across reasoning and code-generation benchmarks.

problem: Multimodal LLMs for GUI automation fail on real-world desktop environments with multi-window stacking, occlusion, and visual clutter due to training on idealized interfaces.
approach: Introduce WinDeskGround benchmark that parametrically generates complex desktop scenarios by controlling window occlusion, layout density, and semantic similarity.
contribution: Evaluates five leading MLLMs on 1,356 instruction-target pairs, showing accuracy declines under partial occlusion.

problem: Existing formal theorem proving approaches rely on task-specific pipelines and trained models, limiting flexibility and reproducibility for diverse mathematical reasoning tasks.
approach: Propose using a general coding agent as a formal math reasoner, combining Claude Code with Numina-Lean-MCP for autonomous Lean interaction and theorem retrieval.
contribution: Solves all problems in Putnam 2025 (12/12) and successfully formalizes the Brascamp-Lieb theorem.

problem: Vision-Language-Action models struggle with few-shot imitation learning and fail to reason about long-horizon tasks with limited demonstrations.
approach: Introduce FOCA framework combining explicit prediction of task-grounded future interaction embeddings with implicit alignment to goal observations.
contribution: Achieves 95.7% success with 20 demonstrations on LIBERO, 7-12% improvement on RoboCasa, and up to 26% gains on real robots.

problem: Editing autonomous driving logs requires simultaneously modifying objects and ego-trajectories while maintaining physical plausibility, creating a dilemma between generative flexibility and precise control.
approach: Introduce SceneDirector using LiDAR-guided depth completion to construct geometric scaffolds and static texture banks, with mask-gated reference attention balancing geometry and appearance.
contribution: Outperforms state-of-the-art in both controllability and visual quality.

problem: Multi-hop question answering must handle both parallel fact-verification and chained reasoning with complementary requirements, yet existing methods excel at only one.
approach: Propose DTKG framework inspired by cognitive science that dynamically categorizes questions then applies tailored reasoning paths for parallel or chained inference.
contribution: Achieves 5.0%-29.5% performance improvement on six datasets.

problem: Learning-based combinatorial optimization requires supervision or expensive gradients while classical approximation algorithms provide guarantees but cannot adapt to input distributions.
approach: Propose fully differentiable MPNN incorporating approximation-algorithmic principles for Uniform Facility Location without solver supervision or discrete relaxations.
contribution: Has provable approximation guarantees and empirically improves on standard approximation algorithms.

problem: Optimizing maintenance strategies for large-scale infrastructure requires offline constrained RL under hard budgetary limits without dangerous exploration, but existing benchmarks lack distributional shift and realistic constraints.
approach: Introduce InfraRL benchmark from U.S. National Bridge Inventory defining offline maintenance strategy optimization under hard budgetary constraints.
contribution: Benchmarks diverse approaches revealing critical trade-offs between safety and long-term efficiency.

problem: Solving discounted MDPs efficiently requires balancing sample complexity without knowing prediction error quality when using external predictions of transitions.
approach: Propose algorithm leveraging predictions of transition matrix without requiring knowledge of prediction error using minimax optimization techniques.
contribution: Achieves sample complexity uniformly better than O((1-γ)^-4 N ε^-2), improving upon prior results despite not accessing prediction quality.

problem: Incomplete multi-view clustering with partial observations relies on weak cross-view signals and overlooks stable neighborhood structures, leading to unstable latent recovery.
approach: Propose IMVC-NCD using neighborhood-conditioned diffusion that aggregates stable local neighborhood structures while encoding missingness states for reliable guidance.
contribution: Produces semantically aligned and view-consistent representations robust to high missing-view ratios.

problem: Existing software agents trained on human-curated data face a fundamental barrier to superintelligence due to limited training data and lack of autonomous learning experiences.
approach: Propose Self-play SWE-RL requiring only sandboxed repositories where LLM agents inject and repair increasingly complex bugs via RL in self-play setting.
contribution: Achieves +10.4 and +7.8 point self-improvement on SWE-bench benchmarks, generalizing to unseen bug descriptions.

problem: Semi-supervised learning must seamlessly integrate paired and unpaired data, but existing approaches rely on heuristics rather than principled likelihood-based frameworks.
approach: Propose learning paradigm integrating paired and unpaired data via likelihood maximization that connects to inverse entropic optimal transport.
contribution: Demonstrates universal approximation property and effectively learns conditional distributions using combined data.

problem: Repository-level performance optimization demands expertise in reasoning about code semantics and software engineering to reduce runtime while preserving correctness, but benchmarks emphasize what to fix not how.
approach: Introduce SWE-fficiency benchmark with 498 tasks on real codebases where agents investigate code semantics, localize bottlenecks, and produce performance-improving patches.
contribution: Reveals top agents achieve less than 0.23× expert speedup, struggling with optimization localization and multi-function reasoning.

problem: Tokenization remains a hardcoded compression step in LLM pipelines despite the trend toward end-to-end architectures, and existing learnable approaches use weak continuous approximations.
approach: Show token boundaries can be learned using score function estimates from reinforcement learning that directly optimize discrete boundary drawing with techniques like time discounting.
contribution: Outperforms straight-through estimates both qualitatively and quantitatively at 100 million parameter scale.

problem: Most video generation models synthesize scenes holistically and lack mechanisms for explicit compositional manipulation and spatiotemporal control of individual elements.
approach: Propose HECTOR enabling hybrid reference conditioning from static images and/or dynamic videos with explicit trajectory specification for location, scale, and speed.
contribution: Achieves superior visual quality, stronger reference preservation, and improved motion controllability.

problem: Large vision-language models exhibit language bias where they over-rely on text while neglecting visual inputs, leading to hallucination rooted in modality misalignment during training.
approach: Propose Language Bias Regularization during instruction tuning and Language Bias Penalty in DPO training to penalize language bias without additional data.
contribution: Consistently improves on ten general benchmarks and reduces hallucination across diverse models.

problem: Long-sequence reasoning in LLMs creates severe KV cache memory bottlenecks, and existing compression methods fail due to rotating queries in RoPE making representative selection difficult.
approach: Propose TriAttention leveraging Q/K vector concentration in pre-RoPE space via trigonometric series to estimate key importance and score keys by position preference.
contribution: On AIME25 with 32K-token generation, matches full attention accuracy with 2.5× throughput or 10.7× KV memory reduction.

problem: Continuous diffusion for categorical data lacks understanding of which tokenization schemes work best for the framework.
approach: Study latent space structure using Kullback-Leibler divergence on diffusion paths and analyze token prediction accuracy, proving FSQ tokenization is optimal.
contribution: Text-to-speech diffusion with FSQ tokens outperforms LLM-based counterparts while being significantly smaller and faster.

problem: Estimating the forest matrix of signed graphs is computationally expensive as existing algorithms designed for unsigned graphs are difficult to extend.
approach: Propose GSCF algorithm based on loop-erased random walks to generate generalized spanning converging forests in O(n) expected time.
contribution: Achieves high estimation accuracy with O(ln) sampling algorithms, scales to graphs with over twenty million nodes.

problem: Code reasoning methods supervise only final outputs and ignore intermediate execution states, leading to reward hacking with inconsistent reasoning.
approach: Introduce StepCodeReasoner with structured print-based execution-trace anchors and Dual-Granularity GRPO for credit assignment at inter-trajectory and intra-trajectory levels.
contribution: 7B model achieves 91.1% on CRUXEval, 86.5% on LiveCodeBench, outperforming CodeReasoner-7B and GPT-4o.

problem: Reasoning video object segmentation limited to fixed initial inputs lacks capacity to actively acquire further visual evidence, essential for resolving complex references in long videos.
approach: Propose VideoSEG-O3 using multi-turn RL framework with temporal-spatial chain-of-thought, SEG-aware logit calibration, and decoupled thinking traces.
contribution: Achieves advanced performance across 8 benchmarks, excelling in long-horizon and complex reasoning tasks.

problem: Existing benchmarks for causal machine learning rely on hand-crafted datasets, leading to brittle and non-generalizable conclusions about method performance.
approach: Introduce CausalProfiler, a synthetic benchmark generator that randomly samples causal models, data, queries, and ground truths based on explicit design choices.
contribution: Provides first random generator of synthetic causal benchmarks with coverage guarantees across observation, intervention, and counterfactual reasoning levels.

problem: Transformers must handle multiple generative processes, but how a single model organizes multiple conflicting world models remains unclear.
approach: Introduce MetaOthello suite of Othello-like games with shared syntax but different rules trained on mixed-variant data to study world model organization.
contribution: Shows transformers learn shared world-state representations, resolve ambiguity through localized mechanisms, and structure representations abstractly beyond surface form.

problem: Federated LoRA methods adopt uniform aggregation breaking under encoder-decoder asymmetry in medical segmentation where encoder handles appearance shifts and decoder handles supervision variations.
approach: Propose Inverse Asymmetric Tuning personalizing module-specific components while retaining shared pathways, with Subspace Orthogonality Regularizer preventing leakage.
contribution: Consistent improvements over federated LoRA and parameter-efficient baselines.

problem: Repository-level code editing requires understanding complex dependencies across large codebases, but existing approaches rely heavily on complex agent scaffolding.
approach: Propose Clean-PR paradigm using GitHub pull requests as training signal, converting noisy diffs into search/replace blocks via reconstruction and validation.
contribution: Achieves 13.6% absolute improvement on SWE-bench Lite and 12.3% on SWE-bench Verified through agentless supervised fine-tuning.

problem: Survival prediction ignores censoring contributions, potentially discarding useful signals when event and censoring processes are coupled.
approach: Introduce latent decomposition learning event-specific, censoring-specific, confounding, and irrelevant information to guide representation learning.
contribution: Consistent gains over baselines on 10 datasets (2 semi-synthetic, 8 real-world) across 4 popular deep-learning survival models.

problem: Active learning for inferring time-dependent vector fields from Lagrangian observer placements typically follows ad-hoc strategies, lacking principled placement guidance.
approach: Introduce BALLAST combining Bayesian active learning with physics-informed Gaussian process surrogate models and look-ahead amendment for sea-drifter trajectories.
contribution: Demonstrates notable benefits of sequential observer placement on synthetic and high-fidelity ocean current models.

problem: Model markets with competing providers and customers have profit opportunities through intelligent arbitrage when capabilities and costs vary.
approach: Conduct empirical study of arbitrage strategies allocating inference budget across providers to undercut market prices.
contribution: Demonstrates simple arbitrage generates net profit margins up to 40% on SWE-bench, with implications for model development and market dynamics.

problem: Existing pluralistic value alignment methods treat value representations as entangled, limiting fine-grained controllability when modifying individual values.
approach: Propose DisAlign framework using information-geometric perspective to decompose representations into consensus and value-specific components via spectral decomposition.
contribution: Consistently improves value disentanglement and achieves more accurate pluralistic value control.

problem: Ad-hoc teamwork requires robust agents that adapt to novel partners without pre-training, but existing methods rely on expensive partner populations.
approach: Introduce UPD generating training partners on-the-fly and selecting adaptively based on learnability criterion without pre-trained populations.
contribution: Consistently achieves strong performance across Level-Based Foraging and Overcooked environments with higher returns and better human-like behavior than baselines.

problem: Diffusion models require Gaussian noise and iterative sampling with latency-accuracy trade-offs, and non-Markovian star-shaped processes lose temporal coherence.
approach: Propose learning Markovian projection of star-shaped forward process enabling learning over broad exponential models, particularly for knowledge distillation.
contribution: Enables few-step or single-step generation while maintaining flexibility across multiple generative tasks.
